title: Our Top 10 Ideal Customers — So Everyone Sees Themselves in One

intelligence.essence: Shawn asked (02:12Z): write the list of our top ten ideal customers, describe all ten, so in all of them everyone relates to one of them. The ranking is Tree's, adopted 2026-10-31: **1 solo service owners · 2 coaches/consultants/freelancers · 3 creators/influencers/affiliates · 4 home-based side-hustlers · 5 community builders · 6 small 2–10 staff businesses · 7 relationship sales · 8 teachers/tutors · 9 busy parents/families · 10 hobbyists/learners/retirees.** Best payers: service owners + consultants. Best referrers: creators + community leaders. Best daily-life: families + hobbyists. Standing frame: **universal market, first customer first** — optimize for everybody in the foundation, optimize for #1 first in launch sequence. The document (`TOP-10-IDEAL-CUSTOMERS-20261109.md`) describes each one — who they are, what they're carrying, what Naya does for them, the moment it clicks — grounded in his words: the 10 Reasons, WHAT ALL HUMANS WANT (learn, earn, grow; pay bills and rent and eat; an assistant to trust; to be acknowledged, loved, appreciated, valued, respected), and #1's "where has Naya been all my life" moment. **Nothing is put on the pricing page** — the list comes back to Shawn for his eye first, including whether it opens the page (his open Top-10-vs-chart-first decision).
intelligence.human_view: As ordered 02:12Z: "I don't know if you remember when I asked you who is our ideal customer — you write the ideal customer, the top ten people that would benefit, define them. Maybe we should write a list, our top ten ideal customers, and then describe all these top ten, so in all of them everyone relates to one of them." And the standing frame from 2026-10-31, his words: "if you understand who we're serving and like who our market is... that just helps with building."
intelligence.child_view: Imagine ten different people walk up to a door. A hairdresser, a teacher, a mum, a man who makes videos, a lady who sells houses, a retired grandad who loves gardening. Each one looks at the sign and thinks — wait, that's me. That's what this list does. Ten doors, one house, and everybody finds their own door.
intelligence.grandma_view: Dear, we wrote down the ten kinds of people this is really for — the hairdresser who does beautiful work and drowns in bookings, the teacher, the busy mum, the man building his little shop after dinner, the grandad who just wants to learn and share what he knows. Each one is written plainly, so when they read it they see themselves. And the first one — the one-person business owner — she comes first, because she needs it most.
intelligence.ai_view: This is the building compass doing its job: the list proves the world market when read whole (work, learning, family, community, creation = everybody with people counting on them), and the order proves the launch discipline (all ten at once with no order builds something generic for nobody). The descriptions are grounded, not invented — the 10 Reasons, WHAT ALL HUMANS WANT, and the #1 moment are his words, and the flags are kept: the ranking is strategic, not measured conversion data; the doc's statistics are unverified and none are cited; "Sarah, 37, beauty business" stays explicitly hypothetical; the 30-person validation trial stays declined and is not re-offered. The list is a description of who we serve, not a claim about who already joined.
